text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said Tuesday its first quarter results were "unsatisfactory," due in part to adverse foreign exchange rates.
"Without the adverse effect of foreign currency, sales would have increased by five percent," it said. Sales rose two percent in the quarter.
Kodak said sales in emerging markets were flat, but it continues to see this area as a source of long-term growth.
Consumer imaging sales were $1.5 billion in the quarter, up three percent from a year ago, while commercial imaging sales were down 16 percent to $1.64 billion.

"Overall, 1997 started more slowly than we expected and the first quarter results are unsatisfactory," Kodak Chairman George Fisher said in a statement. "We need to improve our execution to achieve results which reflect the company's true potential."
